name: flow
notes: Water surface, current, drifted snow: the sand spectrum put through a domain warp, which bends straight crests into flow lines. A stationary spectrum has no large-scale organisation by construction; the warp is the one way to give it some. Rides the SHALLOW RIGID train (dual scatter 0.2, spacing 0.28, n=3) because the warp makes its curves PHASE structure, and a deep train averages independent windows and blends curves away. Measured both ways on this family: three-quarters more delivered contrast on the rigid train at equal ripple (docs/spectral-atlas.md §4). tonal.gain 1.7 is the shallower train's compensation. From the spectral sweep in docs/spectral-atlas.md; levels 30/55/80 are damage DEPTH, not coverage - moderate damage renders as moderate contrast over intact paint. Verified by tools/spectrum-audit.mjs.
